title: The Solitary Reading Cell

features.name: the scholar's desk
features.desc-on-touch: A table set for one reader only. The books lie open, but no one is turning the pages but you, alone, just as the light divides.

features.name: the learning lamp
features.desc-on-touch: You feel light that reaches only one side of the room. The shadow is as important as the illumination—both say something about thinking done alone.

features.name: the pages that learned solitude
features.desc-on-touch: Books filled with margin notes from two readers, now sitting in a cell where one person reads them together. The margins argue with themselves quietly.

features.name: the gap where two chairs used to be
features.desc-on-touch: You measure the distance across the room where once you sat beside her. Now the space is what you read—emptiness as a text.

features.name: the window facing in
features.desc-on-touch: You look through glass that faces inward rather than out. You see the scholar bent over books, and realize you are outside the cell, watching yourself be alone.

inscription: when two readers became one reader, the understanding split into knowledge that has never been recombined

file.name: Divergence_Notes_Unmarked_Second_Hand.txt
file.note: pages where two margins wrote separate opinions about the same passage, now read alone in a cell where agreement feels like a betrayal

reverie.title: REVERIE — in a field, the moment after one chair is carried
narr: You both sat in a paddock once, books open, summer light.
You pointed at a passage. She shook her head—misread it.
The disagreement was small. You laughed. Light gilded her shoulder.
Today you sit in a cell, rereading that passage alone.
Now you understand it her way, and it breaks something to be right.

exits.label: back to the divergence where two shadows learn they cannot be one
into the deeper shelves where solitude becomes its own archive
upward to the high canopy station where silence lives as signal
